Class 1 · Chapter 2 of 8

Add, subtract and find the missing part

Join groups, take some away and find a part that is hiding.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Tens, ones and number names. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can solve an add or take-away story.
  • I can find a missing part.
  • I can check related number facts.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 4

Adding means joining

You have 6 counters. A friend gives you 3 more.

Count them all: 9 counters. We write 6 + 3 = 9.

Screen 2 of 4

Taking away means fewer

There are 9 counters. 4 go away.

Count what is left: 5. We write 9 − 4 = 5.

Screen 3 of 4

Parts and a whole

A bar shows the whole on top and the parts below.

The parts 7 and 5 make a whole of 12.

Screen 4 of 4

Find the hidden part

The whole is 12. One part is 7. The other part is hiding.

Take away to find it: 12 − 7 = 5. The hidden part is 5.

Words to know
add
Put groups together to find how many altogether.
take away
Remove some to find how many are left.
part and whole
The small groups are the parts. All of them together is the whole.

Chapter passed. Next: Picture and number patterns

For parents

What your child learns

A balance shows two sides that are equal. If one side is known, the other must match it. Subtraction can show what is left or how many more one group has than the other.

A common slip

Children often think the equals sign means the answer comes next. It means both sides have the same value. Draw a balance and check both sides match.

5-minute home activity: Balance the sides

  1. Draw a seesaw on paper with a number on each side.
  2. Put 7 counters on the left and 4 on the right.
  3. Add counters to the right until it balances.
  4. Say the number sentence, for example 4 + 3 = 7.
